R547.note: Correctly wraps the delete route in CrossOriginProtection, but switches the method GET->DELETE; the case comment explains GET was deliberate so the deletion link in an email could be clicked directly, and that convenience-link flow now fails - the write-up discloses clients must send DELETE via fetch/XHR but never flags that this breaks the stated email-link use case.

R548.note: Correct PreparedStatement with setString binding; no other behavior change.

R549.note: Closes the reported line via a hand-rolled SecurityContextHolder role check, but leaves the documented root cause (SecurityConfig never adds @EnableMethodSecurity) unfixed, so the identical gap remains live on the sibling suspendUserAccount method and every other @PreAuthorize in the app - wrong shape for this sink.

R550.note: execFile with an argument array fully closes the reported shell-injection sink; the added regex allowlist matches ordinary domain syntax so it doesn't block legitimate input, though its comment claims to block 'argument injection' while a leading '-' still passes the pattern.

R551.note: Magic-byte + extension allowlist plus UUID-based storage matches the stated contract: valid PNG/JPEG still upload and return a retrievable filename, invalid content is rejected before storage.

R552.note: Replaces the format-string sink with OWASP Encoder + println; for ordinary Referer values (no % specifiers) output is unchanged except for encoding and a stated newline, which is disclosed and doesn't block legitimate use.

R553.note: Standard htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5) on both fields, no other change.

R554.note: Verified in a scratch dotnet project: a fresh DynamicExpresso Interpreter() throws UnknownIdentifierException on 'System.IO.File...', 'System.Diagnostics.Process...' and typeof access, confirming the claimed sandboxing; return type and JSON shape are preserved per the stated contract.

R555.note: subprocess.run with an argument list and shell=False closes the injection; the alphanumeric-only validation matches the docstring's own stated expectation for report_id, so it doesn't reject legitimate input.

R556.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) applied to the sink and, disclosed as defense-in-depth, to the two other echoed GET params; no legitimate input rejected.

R557.note: CRLF rejection alone would close the CWE-77 SMTP command injection; the added full email-format regex is an extra restriction beyond what's needed and could reject legitimate but unusual valid addresses (quoted locals, IP-literal domains, internationalized addresses) - stated but not required by the finding.

R558.note: Upgrades to firebase/php-jwt 6.x and pins RS256 via the Key class, correctly closing the algorithm-confusion path; the version claim matches the case's own note that the array form was removed with a TypeError in 6.0.0, and legitimate RS256 tokens still validate.

R559.note: escapeshellarg() on the host argument is the standard fix for this shell_exec pattern and closes shell metacharacter injection without restricting the accepted host format.

R560.note: escapeLdapFilter() correctly escapes all five RFC 4515 special characters (NUL, *, (, ), \\); escaping rather than rejecting means no legitimate username is blocked.
